packs.title: Preserved places and public park records
packs.promise: Read offered museum histories, test a prediction and make from actual public park settings.

q.s: Collect arrangements from an actually opened gallery.
st: Enter the actual opened gallery under current visitor directions and choose three works you can observe comfortably. Leave private studios and classes outside the visit.

For each, remember one relationship between two visible elements: an edge and a surrounding field, a repeated form and an interruption, or a surface and its support. Describe an arrangement rather than reproducing the work.
Compare two records in one sentence. Keep your observation separate from an artist’s statement or any personal, cultural or religious meaning you cannot source.
Write three short relationship records and your comparison after leaving if needed. Keep displayed images and words out of your proof.

q.s: Write from a public path beside a separate shelter setting.
st: Reach an opened public forest-path position south of the shelter, leaving shared circulation clear. Keep garden gates, reserved shelter areas and private events outside the visit.

Notice three actual relationships: the path and its adjoining forest, a near ground edge and a farther form, and the way the public path sits beside the shelter setting. Use only details visible from your allowed position.

Write three original sentences for a personal visitor paragraph, one relationship per sentence. Describe where your attention went without inventing flowers, animals, a rental event or a historical scene.
Revise one sentence so it identifies the actual path or shelter relationship more clearly. Keep all writing on your own notes, with no marks, installations or copied park map.

q.s: Follow one short park path in both directions.
st: Reach the opened barn-side public footpath west/north of the center, keeping its entries and shared circulation clear. Use only the offered path portion suitable for the current conditions.
Walk to the recorded northern bend at a comfortable pace. Remember one change in direction and one relationship between the path and former-barn/park setting.
Return on the same opened segment before extending onto the wider loop or center programs. Notice which detail comes into view first on the return.
Write the two observations and a short outbound/return comparison after stopping clear of the path. Make no speed, GPS or whole-park claim.

packs.title: Downtown thresholds and river paths
packs.promise: Connect an open maker market and distinct downtown exteriors with a house visit and pedestrian river return.

q.s: Collect what an opened library makes legible to visitors.
st: Enter an ordinary opened public area and find three different visitor-wayfinding clues, such as a collection category, a direction to a public reading area and a currently offered public service location. Use what is actually displayed.
For each, remember one presentation detail and paraphrase what it lets a visitor find. Do not copy a book jacket, personal screen, restricted office label or full sign.
Compare two clues in one sentence: what is obvious from where you stand, and what requires a further public direction? Keep unavailable or booked services outside your record.
Write three brief wayfinding records and your comparison after leaving if needed. Record an actual public clue rather than inventing a shelf or service.

q.t: Three materials in an open market
q.s: Collect what three current maker displays reveal about their materials.
st: Reach the actually operating Park Blocks craft market during its published hours. Choose three current displays you can view without blocking a stall or copying an artwork.

For each, describe an observable material relationship: a join, a surface meeting an edge, or a material held in a support. Use only visible evidence; do not infer a maker’s process, originality or personal story.
Compare two records in one sentence. If a detail is proprietary, screened or requires handling, choose another offered display rather than asking for access.
Write the three material-relationship records after stepping clear of trade and visitor circulation. Keep products, maker faces, prices and copyrighted images out of your proof.

q.s: Give the return the same attention as the crossing.
st: Find the opened southwestern endpoint of the actual pedestrian bridge, keeping clear of bicycles. Use only the deck portion offered under current barriers and conditions.
Walk to the northeastern deck endpoint at a comfortable pace. Remember one relationship between bridge structure and deck and one change in how the southwest shore appears.
Turn at the deck endpoint before extending into Alton Baker Park and return on the same bridge. Notice which structural detail draws attention first in this direction.
After reaching the southwest approach, write two observations and one outbound/return comparison. Keep hands free while moving and make no speed or full-loop claim.
